messages:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout at 10% in eu-west-1. p95 latency crossed threshold (980ms > 600ms). monitoring.alert: latency.canary.p95 HIGH. Suggested action: hold and evaluate.
Carol (Release): Holding the rollout. Thanks for the flag. Can we surface the rollback criteria we agreed on for this change window? Need clarity before we escalate.
Alice (Infra): I’m seeing repeated KV cache evictions on several canary instances, memory pressure spikes followed by GC stalls. p50 looks ok, but p95 and tail latencies are bad. Repro logs: ``ERROR kvcache: eviction spike, mem free 120MB``.
Ben (SRE): Do we have customer-impact numbers? Any errors returned to clients or just slow tails? If it's tail latency only maybe we can limit canary traffic instead of full rollback.
Emma (Support): CS: we already have two customers in EU reporting slow responses in their integrations. They called in and want an ETA. We should notify top-tier accounts and post a status note if we rollback.
Carol (Release): Per SLO playbook: if canary p95 > 2x baseline for >3m OR errors >1% -> manual rollback unless auto-rollback enabled. Auto-rollback is disabled for this release (manual gate). Given customer reports + infra signs, I am leaning manual rollback.
Alice (Infra): Agreed. Root cause looks infra-level (kv cache behavior with new kernel flags). Revert to last known-good model server binary v3.1.7 and keep canaries blocked until patch.
Ben (SRE): I’ll run rollback. Confirming authority: Carol, you sign off? Also confirm comms targets (support, sales, status page).
Carol (Release): I sign off. Notify #support, #sales, and create a brief status page draft. Emma, please prepare the customer message. Ben, execute rollback to v3.1.7 and pin.
Ben (SRE): Executing rollback now. Steps: 1) Pause canary traffic slice, 2) Deploy v3.1.7 to canary pool, 3) Validate health checks, 4) Gradually shift traffic and pin. Running command: ``/release rollback --target v3.1.7 --region eu-west-1 --reason \"canary-p95-latency\"``
deploy-bot: Job 558732 started: rollback -> v3.1.7. Stage: canary_deploy. Logging stream: https://logs.internal/558732
Ben (SRE): canary deploy finished, health checks green. Starting traffic shift to 100% canary slice for validation.
Dave (Oncall): Watching metrics now. I’ve rolled a dashboard to compare p95 pre/post. If p95 doesn’t fall under 700ms within 5 minutes, we pause and reassess.
deploy-bot: Job 558732 update: traffic shift to canary=100% complete. No errors in deployment hooks.
Emma (Support): Status draft: \"We detected elevated request latency for customers in eu-west-1 during a canary rollout. We have rolled back the canary to v3.1.7 and are monitoring. No data loss. We will follow up with a detailed update.\" Posting to status page and notifying the top 5 affected customers now. @sales FYI.
Carol (Release): Also, note: release notes freeze until postmortem. We need a formal RCA and recovery timeline. Ben, please create a rollback incident ticket and tag SRE/Infra.
Ben (SRE): Created INC-2026-8421: Rollback to v3.1.7 due to canary p95 latency. Linking logs: https://incidents/internal/INC-2026-8421 and adding owners.
deploy-bot: Job 558732 complete. Canary rollback to v3.1.7 successful. Fleet pin: v3.1.7 enabled. Rollback duration: 8m 26s.
Dave (Oncall): Metrics: p95 dropped from ~980ms to ~210ms across eu-west-1 within 2 minutes of completion. No increased error rates.
Carol (Release): Thanks everyone. Action items: 1) Infra to collect detailed kvcache heap profiles (Alice), 2) SRE to run a dry-run of the kernel flag in staging (Ben), 3) Support to send follow-up to customers when RCA ready (Emma).
Alice (Infra): Will capture heap dumps and attach to the incident.
Emma (Support): Sent customer follow-ups and updated status page to \"monitoring, degraded -> recovered\".
Ben (SRE): Will schedule a post-deploy safety check and coordinate canary re-roll when fix is validated.
Carol (Release): Closing thread for exec updates. Postmortem timeline: 48h initial RCA. If anything changes I’ll reopen or ping here. :white_check_mark:
